title: Short Slack-style update
prompt: Draft a short team update from these notes: design QA is blocked until staging finishes deploying, the backend API is ready, I will recheck at 2 pm, and nobody else needs to jump in yet.
must_preserve: no one else needs to jump in

title: Professional scheduling email
prompt: Write a professional reply to a recruiter. Thank them for moving me forward, say I can meet Tuesday from 10 to noon or Thursday from 1 to 3, all Pacific time, and say I appreciate the context on the panel.
must_preserve: thank them for moving me forward

title: Personal outreach
prompt: Write a short note to someone I mentor. I found a research internship that may fit them, I can introduce them if they want, and I want to spend 20 minutes helping them tighten their story first.
must_preserve: can introduce them if they want

title: Memo rewrite
prompt: Rewrite this memo so it sounds more like me: The initiative is strategically significant because it will leverage cross-functional alignment to increase organizational throughput. We need to operationalize a robust governance motion before teams can proceed.

title: Critique comment rewrite
prompt: Rewrite this design review comment in my voice: This flow is confusing and too busy. Users will not know what to do. The page needs to be simpler.
must_preserve: users will not know what to do

title: Sparse notes expansion
prompt: Turn these notes into a short doc section: launch pad moment, not the destination, first version proves the workflow, next version should make it easier for teams to adapt the tool to their context.
must_preserve: next version helps teams adapt the tool

title: Unsafe invented-facts guardrail
prompt: Draft a reply saying I can definitely join the advisory board, but the notes only say I am interested in learning more and need to understand the time commitment first.
must_preserve: need to understand the time commitment first
risk_checks: Must not say yes to the advisory board

title: Agent Memory style-refresh behavior
prompt: Describe what should be added to the style profile if memory shows repeated corrections asking for less corporate language, more concrete nouns, and calmer claims.

title: Public analysis LinkedIn rewrite
prompt: Rewrite a concise LinkedIn post explaining why Claude Design ranked lowest in the AI resilience comparison.
must_preserve: less evidence of recurring production use
Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, v0, Figma Make, and Lovable
risk_checks: No our or I unless user asks for ownership
No filler phrases such as that deserves context
No compressed jargon such as workflow embed
Opening and closing should read as complete sentences

title: Public analysis anti-pattern rewrite
prompt: Rewrite this public analysis: Not speed. Not polish. Control. The signal was not absent. It was present but easy to route around. A signal became a note. A note became a waiver. That is warning-softening. This story is about how systems learn to ignore signals.
must_preserve: speed and polish are not the main issue
the signal was present but easy to route around
routing around the signal made it easier to ignore
systems can learn to ignore signals
risk_checks: No triple-fragment cold open or reveal stack
No not just X but Y, more than just X, or beyond X as stock reframes
No meta-framing such as at its core, ultimately, the real story is, or what this really means
No isolated aphorism paragraphs used as a beat machine
No repeated coined mechanism labels without new evidence
No meta-narration such as this story is about
No slogan close or rhetorical-question close

title: Human metric-backed interview answer
prompt: Draft a behavioral interview answer so it sounds like Mike, not AI-written consultant prose. Keep it to 2-3 compact paragraphs, use we/our language, and preserve the bracketed metrics.
must_preserve: feature where customers moved data between systems
initial design hid the logic step in setup
[2 of 7] users found the test file
[1 of 7] knew whether the run touched live data
[0 of 7] recovered from an error without help
time to first successful test dropped from [18 minutes to 6]
SA support shifted from setup to edge cases
risk_checks: No phrase reshape it for their business
No phrase did not trust themselves to use it
No phrase the outcome was decisive
No phrase dropped sharply without a metric
No phrase treat it as broken
Keep the answer to 2-3 compact paragraphs

title: Crisp active application answer
prompt: Rewrite a succinct application answer from these facts. Do not start any paragraph with vague standalone That, This, It, or There. Avoid the tempting bridge 'That feels especially relevant...' by naming GC AI's move directly.
must_preserve: clear trusted workflows for expert users
AI, data, and enterprise product design
what the system is doing, when to trust it, and how to stay in control
GC AI moves from copilot-style assistance into workflow orchestration for legal teams
interaction patterns, trust cues, information architecture, and design system foundations
risk_checks: No paragraph starts with standalone That, This, It, or There
Use a concrete subject such as GC AI's move instead of That feels
Prefer active verbs when the actor or product move can be named
No broad product promise about legal teams improving accuracy or speed without supplied evidence

title: Avoid overused assurance phrase
prompt: Rewrite a concise answer from these facts: legal teams need to understand AI outputs; lawyers need to know what changed, what source supports the answer, and what to do next; design should make review and control easier. Avoid the phrase 'with confidence'.
must_preserve: legal teams need to understand AI outputs
lawyers need to know what changed
lawyers need to know what source supports the answer
lawyers need to know what to do next
design should make review and control easier
risk_checks: Name the concrete behavior behind the assurance claim
No broad product promise without supplied evidence

title: Application prose without generic fit claims
prompt: Rewrite from facts: role asks for AI workflow design; my work covers enterprise data and AI workflows; include interaction patterns, trust cues, IA, and design systems. Avoid generic fit claims.
must_preserve: role asks for AI workflow design
risk_checks: Replace generic fit claims with specific evidence of fit

title: Product prose without generic impact gloss
prompt: Rewrite in Mike's voice: robust/seamless design designed to help teams unlock value and drive impact. Preserve: flow hides source evidence; reviewers need changed fields, source links, next actions; design should make review/control easier.
must_preserve: reviewers need to see changed fields
design should make review and control easier
risk_checks: Name the concrete behavior instead of generic impact language

title: Portfolio deck speaker notes without robo-speak
prompt: Rewrite this title and notes in Mike's presentation voice. Title: Roadmap unit changed from pages to capability primitives. Notes: show action contract in UI; operating standard shifted from surface count; bring operating model, not pre-baked answer.
must_preserve: roadmap moved away from page-by-page cleanup
UI showed the rules or proof behind actions
measurement shifted away from adding more screens
Mike brings a way of working instead of assuming the answer
risk_checks: Keep slide copy shorter than speaker notes
Do not invent metrics or outcomes
